claims.text: As-cast HfMoTaTiZr has a density of 10.21 g/cm³.
As-cast HfMoTaTiZr has high strength at room temperature.
As-cast HfMoTaTiZr has high strength at elevated temperature around 1000 °C.
Ti and Zr are lighter alloying elements than the heavier Hf, Mo, and Ta constituents targeted for replacement.
Increasing Ti and/or Zr while reducing Hf, Mo, and/or Ta will lower the density of HfMoTaTiZr.
The proposed compositional modification can maintain phase stability.
The proposed compositional modification can maintain a homogeneous solid solution.
A homogeneous, phase-stable solid solution enables effective solid-solution strengthening.
Reducing the alloy's average atomic weight by increasing lighter-element content lowers its density.
Preserving solid-solution strengthening and phase stability will preserve high strength at room temperature.
Preserving solid-solution strengthening and phase stability will preserve high strength around 1000 °C.
The modified alloy will have a density below 10.21 g/cm³.
The modified alloy will retain strength comparable to as-cast HfMoTaTiZr at room temperature.
The modified alloy will retain strength comparable to as-cast HfMoTaTiZr around 1000 °C.
The intervention is applicable only while secondary brittle phases are avoided and solid-solution phase stability is retained.
The proposed loading boundary is moderate tensile and compressive loading within the tested room-temperature-to-approximately-1000 °C range.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis allows that an appropriate Ti/Zr enrichment may preserve strength, and the uncertainty field states that the acceptable compositional limits are unknown, but the rejection rule says that failure of any modified sample would falsify the hypothesis. A sample outside the unknown viable composition range could fail without disproving the existence of a successful modification.
